summary.executive_summary: This paper proposes two supersymmetric realizations of the Kostelecký-Krauss-Freedman (KF) type Lorentz-violating gauge action in an N = 1 framework. The authors note that the Standard Model Extension is a natural framework for studying Lorentz violation, and that the gauge sector contains a CPT-even tensor Kµνκλ with Riemann-like symmetries. They state that the action S = −(1/4)∫d⁴x KµνκλFµνFκλ is Lorentz-violating because the tensor has a non-zero vacuum expectation value. The central contribution is showing that supersymmetrizing this action can be done via either a chiral superfield or a vector superfield. In the chiral case, they derive that the background superfield must be chiral, imposing the constraint ξµ = ∂µS, and that the K-tensor depends exclusively on the scalar component S. They observe that no ζ-condensate or G-dependence appears in the K-tensor expression. In the vector case, they use a vector superfield to accommodate the background vector ξλ, noting that the content of partners is richer in this case than in the chiral background. They derive the component field actions Sboson, Sfermion, and Scoupled for both proposals. They emphasize that SUSY is readily seen to be broken by the background in both cases, though they do not have elements to decide whether SUSY breaking occurred before Lorentz-symmetry violation. They argue that Lorentz-symmetry violation, as originated at a more fundamental level in the string framework, cannot be dissociated from SUSY. The paper concludes by raising the question of the influence of the Lorentz-violating background on the spectrum, and the need to avoid non-physical excitations such as tachyons and ghosts. They note that the breaking of Lorentz-symmetry signals the violation of the former, and that a model with contemporary breaking of SUSY and Lorentz-symmetry remains to be built. This is a purely theoretical work with no experimental data, numerical results, or datasets, and no bibliography is provided in the supplied text.
